description: Fanmade campaign by Walker Graves. The first scenario, Late Risers, is playable; later scenarios are pending.

story.intro:
After your stay in St. Mary’s Hospital, you awaken in a morgue beneath a mysterious facility. Green gas seeps under a barricaded door. Your possessions lie nearby. Find a way out.
Campaign by Walker Graves (Dr Jack Science); Spanish translation by Los Archivos de Arkham.
story.setup: Start in the Morgue. Lab Omega is in play with 1 barricade (not per investigator). All other locations, Greyson, First Among Many, Suspicious Briefcase, 2 Agency Troubleshooters and 2 Twisted Supplicants are set aside.
story.hidden: You hear a promise of life beyond death. Serve the voice, and time will bring its reward.
story.reagent: A needle in the briefcase injects a glowing reagent into your hand. Remember that you imbibed a cardinal reagent. The briefcase may pass to another investigator who has not done so.
story.resolution1: You awaken in Hibbs’s Roadhouse. Hibbs dismisses your account of the facility as drunken confusion. The Tailors contained the problem. Gain victory experience; record whether you put out a fire.
story.resolution2: You escape into Hibbs’s Roadhouse and learn the facility’s secret. Gain victory experience. If Greyson is in the victory display, the First claimed the facility. Record whether you put out a fire; keep the briefcase if you escaped with it.
story.resolution3: Greyson escorts you to Hibbs’s Roadhouse and explains the Tailors’ work. You earned her respect and learned the roadhouse’s secret. Gain victory experience, record whether you put out a fire, and keep the briefcase if you escaped with it.
story.prologue: Your investigations left you gravely wounded in St. Mary’s Hospital. Weeks of treatment bring no recovery. As doctors prepare an urgent operation, you glimpse a pair of emerald eyes before everything fades.

night.intro:
7:21 PM

Hibbs stares as you wolf down a plate of greasy breakfast food. The burly man takes a moment, then speaks:

“It started about three days back. These strange fogs started rolling through town. Arkham being what it is, most people just assumed something had gone wrong at a factory downriver and went about their business. But then folks started getting sick. Gave folks weird rashes, some sort of disgusting skin thing. Folks by then were starting to get a bit wary, but business kept up.

Then, yesterday, Doc Pickman wandered into Providence Square with a deer’s head fused to his neck. Both heads were screaming. Government types showed up to put a stop to it, but the word was out. By the time we realized the mists were spreading from folks who were badly infected, the suits had already let a lot of troops get too close. Now there’s a bunch of those things wandering around town. Attacking people. And even more of that terrible miasma.

The word on the street is to hole up somewhere safe tonight. Lots of folks practically live here at my roadhouse, so I thought I’d open up and let ’em gather. Honestly, though, I’m worried how much we’ll be able to defend the place.” Hibbs quiets for a beat, thinking.

“You seem like hardy people, friend. If you’re really concerned about the monsters, best thing you can do is help get folks safe. Arkham’s full of places where people might be holing up. If you could round people up and help to shore up some safe havens… well, tomorrow, I’m sure there’ll be plenty of folks happy to help you figure out your memory lapse.”
night.setup:
Gather Night on the Town, the eight Fallen Arkham locations and three Grinning Victims, Haze of Miasma, Ancient Evils and only three Hunting Shadows from The Midnight Masks. Set story assets aside. Put Hibbs Roadhouse, General Store, Orne Library and Bank of Arkham into play, plus one random location from Docks/Advertiser and one from Boarding House/Magick Shoppe (Spanish guide). Start at Hibbs Roadhouse and put four fixed clues on each of the six locations. One of the other two locations is infected at random.

Defend uses the citizen’s numeric value without committed cards or player-card increases, except for Hibbs’s printed permission. Investigators at the testing investigator’s location may place their clues on that location to reduce the difficulty.
night.resolution1:
Things are getting bad out there. You had hoped that your experiences in the facility were exceptional, but it seems as though all of Arkham is swiftly moving in the same direction. It’s possible that no matter what action you take to keep people safe, it won’t be enough against the spreading tide of miasmic corruption.

Unless, of course, you can cut it off at the source. Find where this evil spreads from and stop it. The strange disease-ridden monster that appeared by the general store leaves you thinking — perhaps there’s something around there that serves as the source of it all…
night.resolution2:
You’ve done it. Thanks to you, countless citizens of Arkham will survive the night to come. These creatures, dangerous as they may be, won’t defeat this city. Not tonight.

Despite your victory, you can’t stop the sinking feeling that no matter how many people make it through, it won’t be enough against the spreading tide of miasmic corruption.

Unless, of course, you can cut it off at the source. Find where this evil spreads from and stop it. The strange disease-ridden monster that appeared by the general store leaves you thinking — perhaps there’s something around there that serves as the source of it all…

friends.title: Interlude I: Friends in Low Places
friends.section1:
Rivertown is quiet. With most of the remaining citizens of Arkham holed up, the streets have only flickering street lamps to keep you company. Strangely, the creatures have also vanished, along with most of the choking fogs.

An hour into your exploration in the Rivertown neighborhood, you’re startled by a hand on your shoulder. You turn to strike, but find Hibbs standing with a grin.

“Easy, friend! Heard you were somewhere around here, figured I’d come and lend a hand for a while. It’s the least I could do given all the help you did for me. Just for a while, though. Afterwards, well…”
friends.section2: Hibbs pauses for a moment, staring at the ground. He squares his shoulders and looks you in the eyes. “Actually, no. You got the savvy to have made it past the suits, and you care about this city. You got a good head on your shoulders. City doesn’t need me to keep the Agency’s secrets. City’d be better off if I stick around and help you put a stop to this. Besides, it’s not like you aren’t already in the know. From now on, I’m with you.”
friends.section3: Hibbs pauses for a moment, staring at the ground. He slumps his shoulders and speaks. “After we find you a lead, I head back. Got a lot of folks safe at the roadhouse, but you never know what could go wrong. There has to be someone there to make sure everyone stays put. So I’ll help you search and then return. That’ll leave us square.”
friends.section4:
Rivertown is quiet. With most of the remaining citizens of Arkham holed up, the streets have only flickering street lamps to keep you company. Strangely, the creatures have also vanished, along with most of the choking fogs.

An hour into your exploration in the Rivertown neighborhood, you round a corner and walk directly into a cloud of the glowing haze. Your eyes lose focus, and for a moment, you see through many eyes at once. You see one self weaving robes of flesh and reciting twisted chants. Another howls, and slowly drags itself arm over arm from a deep tunnel into dark woods. Another stares over a corpse and curses fate.

The Plaguebearer stares through darkness at a small blue sphere, dangling below a colossal red palm that drips green ichor from a stigmata.

The miasma recedes, and your self returns.
friends.hiddenGift:
My return draws near.

I grant you this because you cannot stop me.

How can you expect to contain me when you cannot even contain your curiosity?

dawn.intro1:
12:54 AM:

Midnight comes and goes with little progress. The quiet streets of Rivertown seem to hold no signs as to the source of the monstrosities you’ve been fighting against. Just as you’re considering finding somewhere to catch some sleep, your attention is caught by the sound of wheels rattling on unpaved stones. You peer into a nearby alley, and see a man in a doctor’s coat trying to push a wobbling gurney through a side door. A man whose face you recognize.

It takes you a moment to place him, but the mousy figure can only be Doctor West - one of your two attending physicians at St. Mary’s. What is he doing here? At this time of night? With a dead body?

Before you can answer, several cars come barreling down the street. By the time they’ve passed, West is nowhere to be seen.
dawn.intro2:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. To your surprise, Agent Greyson exits the lead car. Before she can turn to address the gathered agents, you run out and flag her down.

“Certainly didn’t expect to see you all here. Can’t be a coincidence, though. We’re looking for Asset Delta-Two. He’s an expert. Might know how to stop all this. Goes by Herbert West. He-”

You interrupt, explaining your connection to the man, as well as what you just saw. Greyson eyes you with surprise.

“Aren’t you full of the unexpected? Well, if you’re up to it, we’re going in after him. What do you say - feel like joining the cavalry?”
dawn.intro3:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. A cruel looking man in a vest exits the lead car, throwing a cigarette onto the ground and grinding it out. He turns to address the gathered agents.

“Listen up, boys. We’ve tracked Asset Delta-Two back to this location. You want payback for all the good men these freaks have killed? For Greyson? Well, Delta-Two knows how to get it. He’s not gonna come easy, so any force short of lethal on the target is authorized. Anyone else could be infected, so kill on sight.” The man grins like a shark.

Either Delta-Two is West, or the doctor is in real danger. Regardless, you need to get to him before these agents do - he might know how you got into this whole mess!
dawn.intro4:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. To your surprise, Agent Greyson exits the lead car. You sneak closer as she addresses the gathered agents.

“Alright, Tailors. We’ve tracked Asset Delta-Two back to this condemned brownstone. We believe Delta-Two knows how we might put a stop to all this. However, he should be considered extremely dangerous in his own right, and is unlikely to come with us willingly. Do what you have to do. Finally, anyone else you run into isn’t cleared for Delta-Two’s experiments. Terminate any civilians you find.”

Either Delta-Two is West, or the doctor is in real danger. Regardless, you need to get to him before these agents do - he might know how you got into this whole mess!
dawn.resolution1:
As two agents pull a furious West out the door, a woman stands above you and points the muzzle of a gun directly at your midsection. “Nothing personal. But you weren’t cleared for any of this.”

Your last moment of life is a flash of gunfire.
dawn.resolution2:
You bolt out the front door of the manor, pulling the doctor with you. “What’s the meaning of all this? Did you lead that monstrosity to me? Did Greyson? God, what incompetence.”

You protest. You’re not an agent. You’re one of his patients, and he has a lot of explaining to do. West stops, and stares you up and down, squinting in the light of the sunrise. “Ah. Impressive. One of my patients? I suppose I’m going to have to fill you in on exactly what’s going on.”
dawn.resolution3:
You bolt out the front door of the manor, desperate to escape the horrors inside. Screaming and gunfire rings out as the sun breaks above the horizon. You watch from a side street as several agents drag West from the manor, bound, bloodied, and unconscious. “Where we taking him?”

“Back to the Brook Facility. He’s got a lotta work to do and questions to answer.”

You need answers, now. The agents have West, and a handle on all this. Which means there’s only one place to go. Back to the facility.
dawn.resolution4:
The terrifying monstrosity gives one last howl, then falls limp to the floor. Looking around, you find an agent’s sidearm. You fire off a round directly into both sides of the creature’s merged heads, just to be sure. West quickly moves to examine the corpse, and you explain you’ve seen this thing dead before, at an agency facility.

“Ah. Pickman, then. His work has certainly borne strange fruit. But I’m sure you government stooges know all about that…”

You protest. You’re not an agent. You’re one of his patients, and he has a lot of explaining to do.

West stops, and stares you up and down, squinting in the light of the sunrise. “Impressive. One of my patients? I suppose I’m going to have to fill you in on exactly what’s going on, then.”
dawn.resolution5:
The first rays of the morning sun stream across your corpse. As you feel the warmth on your skin, you jolt awake. You are lying on the floor of the manor, surrounded by long-cooled carnage. How are you alive?

You need answers, now. The agents have West, and a handle on all this. Which means there’s only one place to go. Back to the facility.
dawn.resolution5Hidden:
Dead.
That won’t do.
My unbinding needs opposition.
The sorcerer’s folly will be your kind’s undoing.
Do what is asked of you.
Rise.

You are mine, now.

Dead? Alive? It does not matter.

Your soul and humanity persist at my whim.

alive.title: Interlude II: Dead or Alive
alive.section1: As you leave the manor, Greyson flags you down. “We’re headed back across town, to the facility. Come on, we’ll give you a ride.”
alive.section2: You watch as the agents pile into cars and peel off across town, headed back to the facility to lick their wounds and plan.
alive.section3: You step into the back seat, where West is sitting bound, as Greyson takes the wheel. You introduce yourself to West, who seems highly uninterested in anything you have to say right up until you mention how you know him…
alive.section4: You step into the back seat, where West is sitting and staring daggers at Greyson as she takes the wheel. He turns to you with a self-satisfied smile, and begins to speak…
alive.section5:
“Unfortunately, we’ll be heading to the same location. The Brook Facility - hidden beneath the city. Startling, I know.”

You explain that you’ve already been, and West looks at you, bemused.

“And they let you leave without filling you with holes? Well done. We have quite the walk back across town, so I suppose you deserve your answers.”
alive.section6:
“Let me start from the beginning. You know me as Dr. West. The world will know me as the man who cured death. I have spent the entirety of my life in pursuit of a process to reverse the flaw of mortality. Some time ago, I was approached by a research consortium about moving my process to their underground facility. Legitimizing my crucial work from its somewhat squalid origins. Of course, I jumped at the chance.

Unfortunately, a week or so back, some of the less scrupulous physicians grew jealous of my startling advances. Dr. Pickman, in particular, talked the imbeciles on the board into appropriating my proprietary serum for his… occult rituals. You’ve seen firsthand how hardy those revitalized by my reagents can be. He and Dr. Robison likely went too far in folding my work into theirs and created a monster. It escaped after multiple attempts, and has managed to infect a good portion of the city with whatever strange substance it derived from. Hence, the intense mutations spreading throughout Arkham. I quit the facility entirely due to disagreements about the use of my serum, and attempted to leave with my remaining pure reagents and notes. I will admit, those reagents didn’t make it out of the facility with me. I hope they are still somewhere within - they may prove highly useful.”
alive.section7:
“Which brings me to where you fit into all of this. My research required a steady supply of those close to death. I ‘worked’ in the intensive care ward of St Mary’s for this purpose. And I must say, you proved ideal specimens.”

You fearfully ask West what he is implying.

“Your worsening condition led to a complicated surgery. When things went wrong, I wasted no time in applying my reagent. It was notable that your corpses didn’t react - I requested your storage in the facility morgue, just in case. I am hesitant to declare success so early, but you may be the most coherent experiments I’ve performed to date!”

This is ridiculous. You point out to West that you were likely in a coma!

“Ah, and I’m sure you’ve exhibited none of the common behaviors of the re-animated. A compulsive curiosity? Intense fortitude - say, surviving gunfire? And certainly not a startling propensity for violence…”
alive.section8:
Your mind focuses on the events of the past day, and your memories prior to waking in the morgue. West was your surgeon in the hospital. You recall seeing a strange green vial on a table during the operation - The same liquid that was pouring into West’s creations.

And then you woke up in a morgue. In a body bag, no less.

Were you… are you… dead?
alive.perks: You know. You’ve known for a while. What you’ve seen with West just confirmed the suspicions you had. But just because you’ve died, doesn’t mean you won’t be able to put a stop to this madness - heck, with everything happening, being dead might be a plus!
alive.good: It doesn’t matter how things appear. You’re alive. Though your body may not be in great shape, you still have your mind - which is more than can be said of the monsters in that house. And it’s that same mind that will get to the bottom of the horrors plaguing this city.
alive.briefcaseEffect: Remove the Suspicious Briefcase asset from the controlling investigator’s deck. Record that West recovered the reagent. Any one investigator may add Herbert West to their deck for the remainder of the campaign. This card does not count against deck size.
alive.hideEffect: Record that you hid the briefcase.
alive.perksEffect: Add the Strength of Flesh story asset and the Death’s Hold weakness to your deck for the remainder of the campaign. These cards do not count against deck size.
alive.goodEffect: Add the Unbreakable Will story asset and The Folly of Man weakness to your deck for the remainder of the campaign. These cards do not count against deck size.

chorus.intro:
6:11 AM:

You make your way across town as quickly as you can. The first rays of morning alight a town huddling in quiet fear. It is eerily silent. No early risers leaving their homes. Not even bird songs disturb the stillness. You focus inward, and relax for a moment.

Then the first horrible note breaks the air.

Somewhere, nearby, a voice sings out a dark and compelling melody. A song of hate and sorrow, resounding through the empty streets. A melody quickly joined by a second voice, then a third. In short order, the song is repeated all across the town of Arkham.

But no matter how you adjust, you can always hear that first voice, above the din. Leading the chorus in its eldritch invocations.

You feel a sting at the base of your skull, and your head goes momentarily fuzzy.

“Rejoice!
Rebirth!
We will all
hear the Call!
of The Bloody Unbinding!
Freedom!
Justice!
Though He dies
he will rise!
with The Bloody Unbinding!”

“The Bloody Unbinding.” You don’t know what it means. But it has to be stopped.
chorus.introHidden:
Rejoice
Disease
They gather
I call you forth
They will break the Seal
Freedom
Revenge
It betrayed me.
It failed.
They will break the Seal
chorus.setup:
Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: Mourning Stroll, Fallen Arkham, Haze of Miasma, The Plaguebearer’s Commands, Locked Doors.

When gathering cards from Fallen Arkham, set all cards other than Grinning Victim aside.

Put each location into play in the following clockwise order, starting with Orne Library: Orne Library, Ye Olde Magick Shoppe, General Store, Arkham Advertiser, Bank of Arkham, River Docks, Hibbs Roadhouse, Ma’s Boarding House.

Check your campaign log. In a random order, for each location not marked as either “Defended” or “Infected”, mark it as the value which appears less.

Check your campaign log. If there are 6 or more “Infected” locations, strike the “Infected” tag from the location of the lead investigator’s choice and mark it as “Defended” (Do this twice if there are 7 total infected locations).

Check your campaign log. For each location recorded under “Defended Locations”, remove the following set aside cards from the game:
• Arkham Advertiser: Bad News, Doyle Jeffries
• Bank of Arkham: Bankrupture, The Vice President
• General Store: Damaged Goods, The Loving Couple
• Hibbs Roadhouse: Intoxicating Vapors, Hibbs (Just Gutted)
• Ma’s Boarding House: Broken Trust, Ma Matheson
• Orne Library: You Know Too Much, Henry Armitage
• River Docks: Worked to the Bone, The Thing in the Water
• Ye Olde Magick Shoppe: Whispers of Power, Miriam Beecher

Add each set aside treachery not removed from the game in this way to the gathered encounter cards.

Check your campaign log. For each location in play that is “Infected”, replace the current location with the location of the same name from the Fallen Arkham set.

Place the Priest of Plagues at a random Miasma location and a Minister of Sickness (ignoring its Forced condition) with 1 doom on it at the next clockwise location. These will form the initial Procession.

The investigators begin play at the Stable location of their choice.

Set Worshipful Thrall aside, out of play.

Shuffle one of the set aside Elite Fallen Arkham enemies and each Infected enemy to form the Procession deck.

Shuffle the remainder of the encounter cards to build the encounter deck.
chorus.procession:
The dark procession marching through Arkham modifies the behavior of the enemies within it.

When you “grow the Procession”:
• Draw the top enemy of the Procession deck.
• Spawn it at the location clockwise of the last enemy in the Procession.
• Place 1 doom on the new enemy.

Ignore both the Hunter and Patrol keywords on enemies in the Procession.

When the Procession moves:
• Move the Priest of Plagues one location in the counterclockwise direction.
• In clockwise order, each other ready enemy in the procession disengages from any investigators and moves directly to the location closest to the Priest with no other Procession enemies in the clockwise direction “following” the Priest. This can cause them to pass over exhausted enemies’ locations.

When an enemy in the Procession would be discarded from play, it is discarded to a separate Procession discard pile. When you would draw from an empty Procession deck, shuffle the Procession discard to form the new Procession deck, and draw the top card.
chorus.defeated: You’re not sure when you joined the procession. You’re not sure how. But you wandered the streets in a daze, signing hymns you learned before you were born. It was beautiful.
chorus.defeatedHidden: Rejoice in fear. I live again. It is only a matter of time.
chorus.resolution1:
As soon as the mortar fire stops, you watch the bloody viscera of the processions’ remains form a strange sigil in the sky. Twisting shapes of green and red, it shifts and pulses like the veins of a living being. You grab hold of the nearest infected, and shake them, demanding an explanation.

“He is freed! He is reborn! They have heard the Call and killed us! Our undoing is his unbinding! The Bloody Unbinding!”

A terrible mistake has been made.
chorus.resolution2:
As the horrid music fades from your ears, you watch the bloody viscera of the priest form a strange sigil in the sky. Twisting shapes of green and red, it shifts and pulses like the veins of a living being. You grab hold of the nearest infected, and shake them, demanding an explanation.

“He is freed! He is reborn! You have heard the Call and killed us! Our undoing is his unbinding! The Bloody Unbinding!”

You have made a terrible mistake.
chorus.hiddenEffect: The first investigator to read this adds one Elder Thing token to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign.

allied.title: Interlude III: Arkham Allied
allied.intro: As you ponder the meaning of the strange sigil emblazoned on the sky, you hear someone calling your name…
allied.hibbs: A group of patrons, half seas over, sing a drinking song with your name awkwardly inserted into it. You can’t help but feel a camaraderie with this motley crew.
allied.store: Davy, the shopkeep of the general store meekly calls you over, and hands you a ratty punchcard. “As far as I’m concerned, you get the best price I can give you on anything you need.” He eyes the sigil with fear. “I’m sure you’ll need it.”
allied.bank: Before you can react, the Vice President of the bank has shoved a case into your hands. You crack it open as he looks nervously at the sigil in the sky, and find it stuffed with cash. “An investment in Arkham’s future.”
allied.library: Professor Armitage produces a tome with gilded pages from a tote bag. “This is one of the most precious pieces in the forbidden collection. I only hope it will assist you in reversing whatever terrible fate these signs portend.”
allied.boarding: The elderly Ma Matheson says very little, but shakes your hand and gives you a tin filled with homemade pastries. Several onlookers eye you with surprise.
allied.shop: Miriam Beecher coughs, and gestures to the sigil in the sky. “This is far from over. I don’t know what you’ll need, but I know a being that may be of some help…”
allied.advertiser: A camera bulb flashes, and you find yourself surrounded by several reporters. “Soon as we’re in the clear, all of Arkham’s gonna want to shake your hand”
allied.docks: You’re lifted off your feet by a group of celebrating dock workers. After some pleading on your part, they drop you, but not before you’re made an honorary union member.
allied.hidden: Your time is nearly up. Even now, my prison fails. When the midnight hour arrives, prepare for your end.
allied.hiddenEffect: Each investigator reading this gains 2 experience and 1 mental trauma.

history.title: Interlude IV: History Lesson
history.lesson1:
Robison walks you along a twisting path, and begins to elaborate. “Let me start with a history lesson. Reality is far more complicated than you or I ever believed. There are beings and species of such magnitude and power that humanity pales in comparison. But, all life shares the same propensity for conflict. Aeons ago, there was a being - a Great Old One known as Baalshandor. Think of him as a twisted god of life. While many of the Old Ones created beings in their image, Baalshandor found his niche in evolutionary chaos. Germs, viruses, bacteria - they were all his children.

The diseases were as much tools as children. Any lesser being infected, will find themselves serving the whims of the Plaguebearer in their idle moments. Many Old Ones abhorred these creations. A being known as Cthugha, obsessed with purity, was particularly offended - Offended enough to war against Baalshandor.

They were evenly matched. Baalshandor could corrupt almost anything, and the fire of Cthugha could burn away any impurity. So clever Cthugha sought aid. An ancient deal was struck, with an entity whose name I dare not speak- I will call him The King. Cthugha would see his ancient enemy destroyed, and the King would gain control over the pestilence of Baalshandor. Together, Cthugha and the King destroyed Baalshandor’s armies.

But Baalshandor could not be destroyed. So a prison was crafted, beyond all known dimensions. It would bind Baalshandor outside of reality - even in all his power, only shades of his virulence were able to seep through. To unbind Baalshandor, he would need a mass sacrifice of followers. As his creations could be culled before this occurred, the Old Ones believed this prison unbreakable.

But I am afraid that to aid my colleague’s search for knowledge, I passed along dangerous rituals to draw upon Baalshandor’s power. Trust me when I say I truly regret it. Not only did it corrupt him, it somehow brought him back from his destruction by Cthugha’s kin. He became a walking extension of Baalshandor, and the bacteria that he spawned spread to the city. It is small comfort that that city is about to burn.

Throughout the ages, whenever Baalshandor’s blood has flowed into our reality, The King and the Flame have been there to destroy all that it tainted. Even now, they prepare a last attack to destroy Arkham and prevent his unbinding. The city will fall, but it will not stop him.

In the hours to come, Baalshandor will emerge from the ashes of Arkham. His children will be endless. In a matter of hours, the earth will be his. And only you can stop it.”

You lose yourself in thought for a moment, then stagger back in shock, terrified of what you see. You stand on a stone ring surrounding a terrifying mass of spheres and eyes.

“An aspect of my master. As a gesture of apology from me, you may ask of him any one question. He may choose to answer more, but beware- few of his offers come without a cost.”
history.portals: Yog-Sothoth is the key and guardian of the gate. He knows where the Old Ones broke through of old, and where They shall break through again.
history.portalsEffect: Record in your campaign log that you saw a vision of the portals.
history.first: There was a formula for evoking such a shade, and another for putting it down; and it had now been so perfected that it could be taught successfully.
history.firstEffect: Record in your campaign log that you learned the killing words.
history.baalshandor: That is not dead which can eternal lie. And in strange aeons, even death may die.
history.baalshandorEffect: Record in your campaign log that you received a cryptic riddle.
history.lesson2:
“I hope you have the answers you seek. Your time here draws short - unless you would prefer to abandon this folly and dwell with me amongst the endless for eternity?”

You shake your head. Arkham’s in more danger than ever. Only you have the knowledge to stop what’s coming.

Robison speaks a few words, and the stars fade from the sky, followed by the rest of the light in this realm.
